Plate tectonics is a very new idea when compared to the other sciences. It only came into vogue around the late 1960s, early 1970s. For reference, most other sciences had their central paradigms established back in the 17 and 1800s.

So what is plate tectonics?

I am going to say some things that might be hard to wrap your head around over the course of the next few posts. The first is that on long enough time scales every solid thing acts like a liquid. Mountains crash like waves, and valleys flow like rivers. They just do it very, incredilby, mind bogglingly slowly.

Now imagine a pot of boiling water. It is being heated from the bottom, so the water at the bottom is hotter than the water at the top. Just like with air, hot water rises (it's less dense) and cold water falls. This creates circular flows of water in the pot as the hot water rises and pushes the cold water out of it's way, while the cold water does the same to the hot water as it falls. This is called convection. We'll come back to this in a bit.

At the center of earth there is a hot chunk of metal that is almost certainly primarily iron and nickel. It is "solid" because the overlying pressure of all the rock on top of it is keeping it from flowing easily. Beyond that there is a sea of liquid iron and nickel. It's the same as the solid part, only the pressure is less strong so it's able to flow. These two zones are called the core of the Earth.

Above that there is a thick layer of jello like rock called the mantle. It flows, but it flows like tapioca more than water. It's mostly made of iron, magnesium, calcium and other heavy elements.

The top layer of Earth is made up of a (relatively) thin crust that is anywhere from 5 - 20 km thick. I think of this like a skin that forms on top of soup when it's allowed to sit for too long.

All throughout these three zones there are radioactive elements like Uranium that are decaying. As they decay they give off heat. Since most of the radioactive elements are towards the bottom of the periodic table they are very dense compared to the other rocks, which means that they tend to sink and collect at the bottom near the core. That means that there is a bunch of heat being released at the core of the earth, and it is heating up the mantle like a stove eye does to water.

The mantle flows, but it is thick, almost solid like gelatin. That means that the bottom of the mantle is hotter (and less dense) than the top of the mantle. The top of the mantle gets pushed out of the way by the hotter mantle from the bottom, and sinks down to the core where it is heated up. This creates a convection cycle within the mantle. So there are these large moving circular flows in the rock that the crust of the earth floats on top of. These convection currents act like conveyor belts that carry the plates across the top of the mantle until the collide with one another or move apart from one another exposing the mantle below.

This is a very basic overview of plate tectonics. I'll be going into more detail tomorrow, and will eventually segue into volcanism.

Thanks for reading.
